  "text": "The key hung at the height of a child’s hand. Rain struck it and ran upward along its teeth.

The constable took a step toward the door. Ada caught his sleeve.

“She isn’t your daughter,” she said.

“I know.” His voice was barely audible. “I locked the gate because she wasn’t.”

Outside, the child stopped in the middle of the street. Water gathered around her shoes without touching them. The five letters reached the stair where Ada had placed the sixth and went quiet.

Venn knelt to read the constable’s name. “There’s a date beneath it.”

“Today?” Ada asked.

He shook his head. “Twenty-three years ago.”

The coat straightened. From inside its hood came the sound of someone drawing a long, patient breath.

“I asked to leave,” it said.

The constable pulled his sleeve from Ada’s grasp. He went to the threshold but did not cross it. “The gate was open in the morning,” he said. “I thought you’d found your way home.”

The key turned once in the air. Behind them, deep in the house, a latch lifted.

Ada looked back. At the end of the hall stood a narrow door she had taken for a cupboard. Wet footprints led from it to the stairs. They were too small to belong to anyone in the room.

The child in the street raised her empty hand, pointing past Ada.

From behind the narrow door, a grown woman called, “Father?”

The constable made a sound like a laugh. The coat reached for him, but Ada caught its sleeve. It was warm."
